newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN names special coordinator on landmines.
newsitem.headline: UN names special coordinator on landmines.

text.p: The Conference on Disarmament (CD) agreed on Thursday to appoint a special coordinator who would look into launching global negotiations to ban anti-personnel landmines.
The consensus decision, reached at a weekly public session and announced by the Slovakian chairwoman, came a day before the United Nations-sponsored forum ends its second session of 1997.

Maria Krasnohorska, the Slovakian ambassador who currently serves as chairwoman, asked the 61 member states to say whether they could accept a draft Western text put forward last week by Australia which proposed naming a special coordinator on mines.
Seeing no objection, she announced: "It is so decided."

Western diplomats had feared Syria and Cuba might hold up consensus on naming a special coordinator to seek consensus on talks on banning the use, storage, production and transfer of landmines. Mines are blamed for causing 25,000 deaths a year.

The Geneva talks had been deadlocked all year due to a row between Western states eager to negotiate global bans on landmines and production of bomb-making fissile material, and non-aligned states seeking greater steps towards elimination of nuclear arms.
